text: You've seen how a purple team exercise gets planned, how it's run technique by technique, and how every action gets mapped to a shared MITRE ATT&CK vocabulary. This lesson closes the loop: what the exercise is actually supposed to produce, and why that output has to be a running rule, not a document.

It's tempting to treat a purple team exercise like a penetration test that produces a report of findings. It doesn't, or at least that's not the point. A finding that stays a bullet point in a slide deck has changed nothing about the organization's ability to catch that technique tomorrow. A finding that becomes a deployed detection rule actually has.

Say the exercise surfaces a real gap: LSASS memory dumping isn't detected. The fix is real detection engineering in Microsoft Sentinel, written in KQL, the same foundation covered earlier in this path — watching process telemetry for the known procdump-against-lsass pattern or the rundll32-and-comsvcs.dll trick, while excluding the organization's own known EDR service accounts to cut obvious false positives before it ever ships.

That rule doesn't go straight from written to trusted. It follows a real lifecycle: build the query from the gap's hypothesis, test it against the actual technique, tune it against real production traffic for false positives, deploy it as a live analytics rule, and document it in a detection catalog mapped to its ATT&CK ID. The loop only actually closes once a re-run of the real technique confirms the new rule fires.

Not every gap ends at a new rule. Sometimes it's a missing telemetry source that never let any rule see the behavior at all. Sometimes it's an EDR prevention policy, turning a detect-only alert into an automatic block. Sometimes it's a SOAR playbook, so the response is already automated the next time the rule fires.

And one exercise is never the end of it. Detection coverage decays as environments change, agents get reconfigured, and log sources get renamed or retired. Mature programs run purple team exercises on a recurring cadence and track real metrics over time — coverage against the ATT&CK matrix, mean time to detect, and whether old gaps have quietly reopened. That's how the detection program stays honest, chapter after chapter.
